reason: This passage (Genesis 22, the Binding of Isaac) portrays Abraham, the most prominent figure of elite status, in a decidedly favorable light. Despite being subjected to a severe trial, Abraham demonstrates unwavering faith and obedience to God. The narrative concludes with God commending his righteousness ('now I know that thou fearest God'), and Abraham receives abundant blessings and promises of progeny. The other figures mentioned (servants, Isaac) are portrayed neutrally or sympathetically. No elite figures are explicitly presented as morally compromised or contemptible.
